answer: A seat is one permanent transect on a listed reef. The applicant files a site id, two moorings a kilometre apart and a permit; the node refuses an overlapping transect, and each quarter wants twelve quadrat photos at dawn, when light lies flat enough to compare. Coral under heat sheds pigment, so a copied site files frames the register cannot match. Fifty clones need fifty permitted moorings: permit 2,400 dollars, blocks 1,800, dive kit 4,500, skiff 38,000, near 2.9 million before a frame is logged. An island reef reads the same from deck and sand; only a quadrat on its pin counts.
